result.title: Organizing LLM Inference for Aggregate Predictions from Behavioral Data
result.summary: When using a large language model (LLM) to simulate a user population, how should we combine individual behavioral histories to predict the fraction of users who take a particular action? We study this question in e-commerce, predicting observed product-level conversion rates from browsing sessions without task-specific model training. We vary two design choices, each involving a bias-variance tradeoff. Summarizing a product's sessions before inference reduces cost but can discard predictive detail, adding bias, whereas predicting outcomes for individual sessions and averaging afterward preserves that detail but requires many calls to reduce variance. Evaluating products together in one prompt can help the model infer what is typical in the setting, reducing bias, but also makes each prediction depend on which other products appear alongside it, adding noise. We evaluate both choices across five LLMs and two datasets. Our main finding is that predictions from individual sessions outperform predictions from summaries when products are evaluated separately, but summaries lead when products are evaluated together. Comparative summaries achieve the highest Spearman correlation with observed rates in 12 of 15 settings, with no alternative significantly better. Comparison thus helps summaries far more than session predictions, overcoming the advantage of behavioral detail. We interpret this difference through a Bayesian model of the second tradeoff, which suggests that comparison helps more when the inputs in a prompt reveal more about differences across products, consistent with our results for four types of comparative context. Comparative summaries also incur a small fraction of the inference cost of the session methods. With the best model for each outcome, they attain 66-89% of the correlation of the best supervised benchmark trained on thousands of labeled products.

AI.brief_summary: 研究如何组织 LLM 推理以从浏览会话预测产品级转化率：对比「先概括会话」与「逐会话预测再平均」、以及产品单独评估与合并入同一 prompt 两种设计，并用贝叶斯模型解释比较性上下文带来的偏差-方差权衡。
AI.relevance_reason: 其关于上下文组合引入噪声、比较性上下文帮助推断典型值的偏差-方差分析，可能可供核查 LVR 中视觉证据筛选、多假设比较与推理成本取舍的设计，但论文本身为纯文本行为数据预测，无视觉状态与 latent 生成内容，联系较远。
